newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Thursday in what traders termed a brief correction.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.71 percent, or 5.21 points, to 298.74 on a moderate all-share turnover of 185 million shekels against 210 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.76 percent lower at 303.63.

"It's only normal that after the market rose to new highs investors take profits," said Jacques Goldhar head of international activities at Jerusalem Capital Markets. "The market is still very good and foreign investors are also showing interest. I believe that the market will resume its rise next week."
Goldhar added that the Dow's fall created negative sentiment on Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial ended down 119.88 points, or 1.51 percent, at 7,842.43 on Wednesday.
A trader at the First International Bank of Israel agreed that the market's decline would be short-lived. "It's only a correction and I believe that the market will resume rising on Sunday," he said.
"Mutual funds are raising more money to invest in the stock market," Goldhar said. "In the long run the trend is still very positive."

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which gained 1.0 percent to 34,665 agorot on volume of 18.6 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which fell 1.0 percent to 564 agorot on turnover of 11.6 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which closed unchanged at 777 agorot on volume of 8.3 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
